headline: Two confirmed intrusions credited to AI-driven attackers (Bell Canada, and Cairn-assisted attacks on universities); a third-party vendor breach reaching Chase, Visa and Mastercard customers; a $13.5M key-compromise drain at Wagyu (XMR1) on Hyperliquid; and four newly confirmed exploited flaws, led by a VMware vCenter zero-day tied to a China-linked group.

incidents.what: Says an "agentic" threat actor breached its systems on Nov 17 and stole enterprise customer data, including from a circuit-provisioning system.
Customer personal and marketing data exposed through a cyberattack on a third-party service provider.
Deployer signing key taken via a breach of third-party hosting; 5.2M XMR1 moved and sold into Hyperliquid's order book.
Multiple applications taken offline over several days in response to a cybersecurity incident.
China-linked actor used the open-source AI pentest framework Cairn against two universities, possibly finding a zero-day.
More than 40 breach notifications after a Belfast-based data processor was breached, unnoticed for six weeks.
Attackers who breached a server caused a worldwide outage of Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud.
Breach added to Have I Been Pwned.
CVE-2026-123890 auth bypass, exploited as a zero-day since September by China-nexus Armory Castle; added to CISA KEV.
CVE-2026-76466 exploited shortly after a public proof of concept to breach devices and reach an internal network; added to CISA KEV.
